messages.text: Brilliant sprinter Almeraq retired to stud

metadata.summary: Champion sprinter-elect Almeraq has been retired to stand at Shadwell's Beech House Stud for 2027.
metadata.content: Brilliant sprinter Almeraq retired to stud | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Brilliant sprinter Almeraq retired to stud Less than a week on from his brilliant exploits in the Champions Sprint, Shadwell Stud have made the decision to retire Almeraq. Wednesday 21 October 2026 18:16, UK Image: Tom Marquand and Almeraq enter the winners' enclosure Champion sprinter-elect Almeraq has been retired to stand at Shadwell's Beech House Stud for 2027. Winner of three six-furlong Group Ones this season for William Haggas and Tom Marquand, that would be a a remarkable season in any book before even considering what happened to him at the end of the 2025 season. Running in a Listed race at York in September he clipped heels and took a very heavy fall. Connections feared the worst yet while the horses emerged generally unscathed, neither jockey involved, the now-retired Jim Crowley or Trevor Whelan, have ridden since. For Almeraq to bounce back this season to not only win races but at the very highest level, shows another side to his character. Ombudsman strikes Champion Stakes gold | Full replay Darkness Falls strikes Dewhurst gold for O'Brien The four-year-old by Dark Angel won the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot, the Haydock Sprint Cup by over four lengths and on Saturday he took the British Champions Sprint. messages.text: Conan, Doris, Crowley absent from Ireland's Nations Championship squad

metadata.summary: Andy Farrell's Ireland will head into November's Nations Championship without injured trio Jack Conan, Caelan Doris and Jack Crowley, but Jamison Gibson-Park has been included.
metadata.content: Nations Championship: Ireland without injured trio Jack Conan, Caelan Doris, Jack Crowley but Jamison Gibson-Park included | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship: Ireland without injured trio Jack Conan, Caelan Doris, Jack Crowley but Jamison Gibson-Park included Jack Conan, Caelan Doris and Jack Crowley will miss Ireland’s Nations Championship Tests against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa next month due to injury; Jamison Gibson-Park has been included despite his recent groin problem, while Mack Hansen and Andrew Porter return to the squad Michael Cantillon Sports Journalist Wednesday 21 October 2026 16:44, UK Image: Jack Conan (left) and Caelan Doris (right) have both been ruled out of Ireland's Nations Championship Tests in November through injury Andy Farrell's Ireland will head into November's Nations Championship without injured trio Jack Conan, Caelan Doris and Jack Crowley, but Jamison Gibson-Park has been included. Ireland face Tests against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa next month without captain Caelan Doris and fly-half Jack Crowley, who are both expected to return from long-term injuries in January. Doris has been sidelined by foot and knee problems, while Crowley is recovering from a vascular issue in his leg. Conan, who like Doris plays at No 8, is also ruled out after injuring his shoulder while playing for Leinster in the Champions Cup last weekend. messages.text: McCullum on Brook: Our relationship has really blossomed

metadata.summary: England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum believes leaving Test cricket in the rear-view mirror has allowed his relationship with Harry Brook to continue to flourish.
metadata.content: England cricket: Brendon McCullum believes his relationship with Harry Brook has 'blossomed' over the past 18 months | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive England cricket: Brendon McCullum believes his relationship with Harry Brook has 'blossomed' over the past 18 months As England engage in a rare tri-series tournament, white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum reflects on his time as Test coach and heaps praise on white-ball captain Harry Brook; watch England vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8.30am (first ball 9am) Thursday By Matthew Wolfe Wednesday 21 October 2026 19:20, UK Image: Brendon McCullum and Harry Brook during a net session before England's opening tri-series match against Pakistan England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum believes leaving Test cricket in the rear-view mirror has allowed his relationship with Harry Brook to continue to flourish. The New Zealander took charge of the Test side in 2022 and took control of all three formats in 2025. However, in July, a month after then captain Ben Stokes' dramatic international retirement, he stepped away from the Test game that had become such troublesome terrain. "In a funny way, I think, sort of now, Harry and I, our relationship as the captain and coach over the last 18 months or so has really blossomed, and I think we work fantastically well together," McCullum told Sky Sports.
